sentence: This project uses magnetic resonance to follow how muscle disease progresses in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy who receive gene therapy.
This project tests a treatment that uses lipid nanoparticles to deliver mRNA in mouse models of rheumatoid arthritis.
This project uses brain imaging data and predictive modeling to look for biomarkers of disruptive behavior in children with and without autism spectrum disorder.
This project studies how tumor-initiating cells in squamous cell carcinomas resist immunotherapy and reprogram their immune suppressive microenvironment.
This project builds a 3D bioprinted model with disease-specific cells to study how hypoplastic left heart syndrome develops in humans.
This project develops a biomarker that images neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how human regulatory T cells suppress tumor-reactive T cells and looks for ways to control that suppression.
This project develops a microscopic holography method that can reveal chemical signatures and structural dynamics of biological specimens.
This project develops an electrophysiology system to study how changes in cells and molecules in human brain organoids affect their neurons and circuits.
This project tries to make woodchucks susceptible to hepatitis B virus infection by modifying either the virus or the host.
This project uses machine learning to study how sex hormones relate to the structure and function of the developing brain during puberty.
This project studies how ligand binding, nucleotide hydrolysis, and product release are linked to nucleic acid transformations by proteins.
This project builds a deep learning algorithm that uses cervical images to reach a diagnostic result for cervical cancer screening.
This project uses genomic analyses and predictive modeling to study how pathogens spread among wildlife and human settlements.
This project studies how pluripotent stem cells are established in embryos, retained into adulthood, and regulated to form differentiated cell types.
This project tests approved and investigational agents on organoid models made from patient-derived tumor tissues to find which tumors respond.
This project develops nanobody-based therapies and uses human cardiac organoid models to study how amyloid fibril deposition disturbs mitochondria and calcium.
This project studies how proteins raised in colorectal cancer promote tumorigenesis and develops them as liquid biomarkers.
This project studies how a Parkinson's disease risk gene affects the membrane properties and vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons.
This project studies how the autophagy pathway and toll-like receptor signaling help cells make and release defensosomes, vesicles that neutralize bacterial toxins.
